NKE.rationale: Nike is in a severe fundamental deterioration with no credible near-term re-rating catalyst. Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with operating income collapsing to $650M from $844M YoY. Operating cash flow plunged 76% YoY to $430M. Gross margin compressed 130bps due to tariff headwinds, and operating margin has fallen to just 5.8% (from 7.5% a year ago). Net margin is now 4.8%, down from 7.0% a year ago. The company is losing market share — global athletic footwear share fell to 22.9% in 2025, down ~3pp YoY, with third consecutive year of decline per Euromonitor. Competition from On Running, Hoka, and Adidas is intensifying. Short interest has surged to 4.67% from 0.41% at CEO Hill's appointment. The stock trades at 31x diluted PE despite a deteriorating earnings trajectory — this is expensive for a company with no demonstrated top-line growth since FY22 and declining margins. Management has pushed back the growth recovery timeline to Q2 FY2027. Legal overhang from IEEPA tariff refund class action ($1B at stake) adds further risk. News sentiment is deeply negative (mean -0.39 over 90 days). The stock is down 26% in the last quarter alone, trading near 12-year lows, yet the PE multiple remains elevated relative to the earnings power. Q4 FY2026 earnings on June 30 is a potential catalyst but likely to confirm continued weakness rather than inflection. All three pillars — deteriorating fundamentals, expensive valuation vs. deteriorating earnings, and no positive near-term catalyst — align negatively.
